picks.why: Family winery at the foot of Olympus, at Rapsani since 1991 and farmed organically by several accounts; its Rapsani Old Vines is the appellation's three grapes from old vines, aged in oak.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Confirmed in the thin run: Rapsani Old Vines is sold as PDO Rapsani by a Canadian review site (the 2022), two British merchants (the 2019) and a Greek one, and a British critic's site reviewed the 2022; one merchant gives eighteen months in French and American oak and six in bottle, one account plants the vines in 1952, and a Greek travel site says Xinomavro can reach seven parts in ten of the blend. The house also bottles a plain Rapsani (the 2023 is on sale in Britain) and a Rapsani named Tourtoura Old Vines (the 2020 reviewed by the same critic's site): confirm from the house which is the wine to know, and send the others to others with the Meth'Imon wines, whose appellation the author confirms. The dates disagree and the author settles them: at Rapsani since 1991 by several listings, organic from 1997 by one, and bottling the appellation's wine since 2008 by another, so leave founded empty unless two agree on what 1991 was. The lane's site name (Prosilia) was not confirmed, and the altitude (550 to 700 metres by the listings) is the house's own. The Ministry of Rural Development's file of an application to amend the Rapsani specification, named for 30 July 2026 and seen only through search summaries, names this house's company: read it before writing the making or the grapes' shares. Name no living member of the family.

picks.why: Rapsani family estate whose first vineyard was planted about 1935 by its own account, with a small winery set up after the third generation took over in 2002; its Rapsani is the three grapes fermented together and aged a year in old oak.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. The house writes itself under a living man's name: a house keeps its name, but the prose names nobody. Confirmed in the thin run: the wine is sold as Rapsani by a Greek merchant and a British one (the 2021), and a British critic's site reviewed the 2019, the 2020 and the 2021 as Xinomavro, Krassato and Stavroto; the Greek merchant gives the three grapes fermented together and twelve months in old oak. About 1935 and the takeover of 2002 come from two merchants' profiles that read as the house's own words: hedge them as the house's account, and leave founded empty unless an independent source agrees. Sources write the house as Konstantinos Liapis, Liapis, Liapis Winery and Domaine Liapis: confirm the name the label carries, and that the label says PDO Rapsani. A Greek Master of Wine's account of 2016 has the head of this house working the vines of Terra Olympus, the Thymiopoulos company at Rapsani: say it only as two sources agree. Name no living person.

picks.why: The Rapsani company of the Naoussa house Thymiopoulos, set up about 2015 and, by one account, given its own cellar in a restored warehouse near Rapsani's railway station; Terra Petra is its Rapsani, Xinomavro with Krassato and Stavroto, sold under the Thymiopoulos name.
picks.note: IN DOUBT, for the merge agent to rule. Thymiopoulos Vineyards is Naoussa's pick in plan.json (p-thymiopoulos), and that pick's note sends the Rapsani wine to others under the rule of one flagship a producer; the library's record of that house lists Rapsani Terra Petra among its wines. The company is entered here under its own name because three accounts make it a house of this appellation in its own right: a Greek Master of Wine's report of 2016 (the company is called Terra Olympus, and the 2016 vintage was to be made in its own winery in a restored warehouse near Rapsani's railway station), an importer's catalogue (established in 2015, when vineyards within the appellation came up for sale) and the Ministry of Rural Development's file of an application to amend the Rapsani specification, named for 30 July 2026 and seen only through a search summary, which names Terra Olympus of Rapsani. If the rule holds, drop this pick and the group stands at three; if the pick stays, amend the Naoussa note and keep producerId empty here. The wine is confirmed: Terra Petra is PDO Rapsani in an Austrian magazine's review of the 2015 and Rapsani in a British magazine's of the 2017 and the 2018, both under the Thymiopoulos name, and merchants in Greece and France stock the 2019 and the 2020. The author confirms what the label carries (Thymiopoulos, Terra Olympus or both), the grapes' shares (seven parts Xinomavro to three of Stavroto and Krassato by one Greek merchant, which sits beside the equal thirds the Codex's region record teaches: read the specification) and how the vines stand between this company and the Liapis family. Name no living person.

picks.why: A house at Rapsani's railway station, growing vines on Olympus since 1880 by its own account, known at home and little seen abroad; its Rapsani is the appellation's three grapes aged in oak, bottled beside a limited edition.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS and not in the region record's producers line. IN DOUBT, thin: no search of the thin run showed the house at work after about 2022, and no merchant's listing of a recent vintage was found. What was confirmed: a blog post of 2009 that reads as the house's own announcement (growing and making wine since 1880, a fourth generation, a Rapsani of Stavroto, Krassato and Xinomavro aged twelve months in French oak); a Tempi tourism site's page on the wine route (gotempi.gr), which lists it at Rapsani beside Dougos and Liapis; a Greek travel site's guide of about four years ago (two labels, a Rapsani PDO red and a Rapsani PDO special edition, both aged in oak, and the address at Rapsani's railway station); and a Greek Master of Wine's note on the Rapsani 2009 Limited Edition, tasted in January 2020. The author confirms from the house that it bottles today, the label's own words and spelling (Chrisohoou in two sources, Chrysochoou in others), 1880 from a second source or leaves founded empty, and the blend. It is not the Chrysohoou estate of Naoussa, a different house whose wines turn up in the same searches. The group stands at four, not five, and the merge agent rules. Tsantali, the lane's first pick, is dropped as closed: it stopped production in September 2023 and its bankruptcy was entered in the commercial registry on 12 January 2026, by two Greek business reports, so no house makes Rapsani Reserve or Grande Reserve under that name today. The only other bottler found is Boutari, whose own site lists a Rapsani of 2022, and Boutari is Naoussa's pick. Katsaros, which one glossary lists here, is at Krania, which has its own PGI. Name no living member of the family.
